title: Can we formalize the generalized Wilson theorem for prime powers: $(p^k - 1)

problemStatement.formal: For n >= 2, the residue of (n-1)! in ZMod n classifies the prime case, the exceptional n = 4 case, and composite n > 4; for n >= 3, the units-product criterion gives the Gauss-Wilson classification.
problemStatement.plain: Strengthens Wilson-style primality metadata by recording the complete factorial-residue classification. Prime moduli give -1, the exceptional modulus 4 gives 2, and all other composite moduli above 4 give 0; the file also connects to the Gauss-Wilson units-product theorem.
whyMatters: Wilson's theorem is a classical primality criterion, and the complete residue classification explains exactly what happens outside the prime case.
The ZMod formulation makes the statement usable in modular-arithmetic proof search.
The Gauss-Wilson classification links factorial residues with the structure of the unit group modulo n.

proven: `wilson_complete_classification` splits n >= 2 into prime, n = 4, and composite n > 4 factorial-residue cases.
`prime_iff_factorial_neg_one` records Wilson's theorem as a biconditional primality test.
`gaussWilson_classification` characterizes when the product of units modulo n is -1 modulo n.
Concrete native-decision examples verify the composite factorial-zero behavior for several small moduli.
open: Companion entries discuss Wilson-prime refinements; this entry is scoped to the theorem-backed classification file.
